overview: After 1.Nf3 Black plays 1...f6, preparing ...e5 and ...Nh6, but weakening the e8-h5 diagonal and blocking the knight. White typically takes the centre with 2.e4 or 2.d4 and gets easy play and space. Black's Drunken Knight manoeuvre ...Nh6-f7 is slow and odd.

white_ideas.idea: Take the centre with e4 and d4
Develop freely and exploit the weakened king diagonal

black_ideas.idea: Rebuild with ...d5 or ...c5 once the king is safe

typical_structures.structure: White central pawns on d4/e4 against a Black f6/e7 set-up

character.notes: An eccentric defence that cedes the centre.

soundness.notes: Black's set-up is passive and loosens the king, so White stands better.

structure.notes: Flexible: White takes the centre while Black decides how to challenge it.

approach.notes: Seldom played by strong players, chosen for surprise.

level.notes: Little theory, but the line is not a good repertoire choice for Black.

sublines_that_differ.name: Drunken Knight
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. Nf3 f6 2. e4 Nh6 3. d4 Nf7
sublines_that_differ.how: Black re-routes the knight to f7.

character.reason: Quiet but loosened play; neither safe nor forcing.

soundness.reason: The set-up concedes the centre for little.

structure.reason: The centre is not settled early.

approach.reason: Almost never played by strong players.

level.reason: Not for beginners because it is dubious.
